chunks: This is their retribution because they denied Our signs and said: 'When we are bones and crushed bits, are we indeed to be raised as a new creation?'
ai.seo_question: What was the specific claim of disbelievers regarding resurrection that this verse addresses?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Isra underscores the logical consistency of divine power over material decay, countering the disbelievers' skepticism with the assurance of a 'new creation' (khalqan jadidan). It serves as a foundational argument for bodily resurrection, emphasizing that God’s ability to recreate is not limited by the disintegration of bones and dust, a theme central to Shia theological debates on the nature of the afterlife.
